title: Modified Juvenile Reciprocal Social Interaction Protocol
author: Siddharth Singh
materials: From the scored data, define key metrics:

steps.title: Prepare Subjects and Dyads
steps.instruction: Organize juvenile mice (P23-25) into same-sex, same-age dyads consisting of all pairwise combinations of same-group and mixed-group pairs.

substeps.instruction: Ensure mice are raised in >3 litters per group with balanced sex and age.
Assign each subject to a single dyad to avoid repeated testing effects.
Spread littermates evenly across dyad types and randomize pup assignment to groups/dyads.
Aim for ≥10–15 dyads per comparison (power >0.8, α=0.05, β=0.8).
Weigh and record the weight of all mice to ensure they are in a similar range.
Mark mice with non-toxic fur dye or tail marks for identification using gloves and gentle handling.

steps.title: Pre-Test Handling and Habituation
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice for the social interaction test through controlled isolation and habituation.

substeps.instruction: Keep dyad partners in separate home cages (different litters) until testing.
Handle each mouse gently for a few minutes on the day of testing.
Singly house each mouse for ~30-60 min immediately before the test for brief habituation.
Optionally, allow each subject a 2-5 min exploration of the empty arena alone, then remove and wait a few minutes.

steps.title: Set Up Testing Arena
steps.instruction: Prepare the physical environment for the interaction session.

substeps.instruction: Place clean bedding in the arena.
Turn on the camera and verify the view.

steps.title: Conduct Social Interaction Test
steps.instruction: Execute the 10-minute interaction session between the dyad partners.

substeps.instruction: Optionally place Subject A alone in the arena for 1 min to acclimate, then briefly remove Subject A.
Allow subjects to freely interact for a fixed 10-min session, recording with a synced stopwatch and video.
Monitor closely for aggressive behavior (prolonged fighting with bites or injuries); if observed, immediately stop the session and separate the mice.
At 10 min or upon termination, remove both mice and return them to their home cages.

steps.title: Clean Arena
steps.instruction: Clean the arena and allow it to dry completely before starting the next trial.

steps.title: Score Behaviors
steps.instruction: Analyze the recorded video using a directional ethogram where one mouse is the actor (initiator) and the other is the receiver.

substeps.instruction: Assign points based on the Point Metrix system (Table 1) for social behaviors.
Note non-social behaviors (e.g., self-grooming, rearing, digging) as controls without assigning social points.
Apply the Short-Event Rule: count interactions <0.5 sec as a minimum duration of ~0.1 sec.
Score nose-to-nose sniffing as mutual; treat side sniffing as directional.
Calculate Total Active Social Time (T) as the sum of durations of all social interactions per subject.
Calculate Total Social Points (S) as the sum of actor points from Table 1.
Calculate Initiation Count (I) as the total number of events where the subject was the actor.
Calculate Avoidance Duration (A) as cumulative time spent avoiding the partner (1 point per second).

steps.title: Calculate Symmetry and Asymmetry Indices
steps.instruction: Compute the following indices for each dyad (Subjects A and B) using the difference-over-sum formula:

substeps.instruction: Interaction Symmetry Index (ISI) = (S A - S B )/(S A + S B )
Initiation Symmetry Ratio (ISR) = (I A - I B )/(I A + I B )
Non-social Asymmetry Index (NAI) = (G A - G B )/(G A + G B ) where G represents points for self-grooming/exploration.
Duration Ratio Index (DRI) = (T A - T B )/(T A + T B )
Avoidance Asymmetry Index (AAI) = (A A - A B )/(A A + A B )

description: Pair Introduction (t=0): Gently introduce Subject B into the arena at a standardized location opposite to where A was placed (or release simultaneously). Start video recording immediately.
